description: The GEM Building Taxonomy is the Global Earthquake Model Foundation's uniform scheme for describing and classifying buildings in the same way around the world, as a step towards assessing their vulnerability and risk. It characterises assets by attributes that influence the likelihood of damage from natural hazards; version 4.0 has 15 attributes, including main construction material, lateral load-resisting system, earthquake-resistant design, date of construction and number of storeys. The repository provides the attribute tables as a spreadsheet, and GEM offers an online tool to validate and explain taxonomy strings, a Python package (oq-gem-taxonomy), structure and graph views, and a glossary, which is still aligned with version 2. Coverage: global building stock. Access: tables on GitHub and tools on openquake.org. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): AGPL-3.0. Access is free of charge. Caveats: strings from older versions need translation to version 4.0. Simulation uses are the common classification that links building exposure inventories to fragility and vulnerability functions in earthquake and multi-hazard loss models. Related records: the OpenQuake engine, the GEM exposure and vulnerability models, and the World Housing Encyclopedia.
